subject: surgery
title: Surgical site infections, necrotizing soft-tissue infections, and antimicrobial prophylaxis

steps.tx: Surgical **infections** are stratified into superficial incisional, deep incisional, and organ/space infections by CDC criteria. Superficial infections involve only subcutaneous tissue within 30 days of operation. Deep infections involve fascial and muscular layers. Organ space infections involve anatomical cavities manipulated during surgery. Preoperative antimicrobial prophylaxis must be administered within 60 minutes prior to surgical incision to achieve peak tissue bactericidal levels.
steps.say: Surgical site infections are classified into superficial incisional, deep incisional, and organ space categories. Prophylactic antibiotics should be infused within 60 minutes prior to surgical incision to guarantee bactericidal tissue levels during tissue division.

steps.tx: Necrotizing **fasciitis** represents a life-threatening surgical emergency characterized by widespread subcutaneous and fascial necrosis with relative sparing of underlying muscle. Type I is polymicrobial involving anaerobes and enterobacteriaceae; Type II is monomicrobial driven by group A Streptococcus. Clinical hallmarks include pain out of proportion to physical exam findings, dusky skin dishwater pus, wooden hard subcutaneous edema, and cutaneous bullae.
steps.say: Necrotizing fasciitis causes extensive subcutaneous necrosis. Type one is polymicrobial with anaerobes, while type two is caused by group A Streptococcus. Clinical features include pain out of proportion to physical signs, dishwater exudate, and tense wooden edema.

steps.tx: The Laboratory Risk Indicator for Necrotizing Fasciitis (**LRINEC**) score facilitates early distinction of necrotizing infections from simple cellulitis. The score evaluates six routine serum biomarkers: C-reactive protein, total white blood cell count, hemoglobin, sodium, creatinine, and fasting glucose. A score of 6 or greater raises high suspicion, while a score of 8 or greater carries a positive predictive value exceeding 90 percent.
steps.say: The LRINEC score differentiates necrotizing infections from simple cellulitis using six parameters: C-reactive protein, white blood cell count, hemoglobin, sodium, creatinine, and glucose. A score of six or more warrants urgent surgical evaluation.

steps.tx: Definitive management of necrotizing soft tissue infections hinges on emergency **surgical** debridement down to viable bleeding tissue without awaiting imaging results. Broad-spectrum empiric parenteral antimicrobial coverage with vancomycin, piperacillin-tazobactam, and clindamycin must be initiated immediately. Clindamycin functions as a ribosomal protein synthesis inhibitor that suppresses staphylococcal and streptococcal toxin production. Planned second-look debridement is mandatory within 24 hours.
steps.say: Management of necrotizing fasciitis requires immediate surgical debridement down to healthy bleeding tissue. Empiric antibiotics must include vancomycin, piperacillin tazobactam, and clindamycin to halt bacterial toxin synthesis. Mandatory re-exploration occurs within 24 hours.
